# kick-off

Turn the owner's intent into merged work: one manager per project routes it, workers define and do it.

Arguments: worker replay-worker manager replay-manager task 1020, Follow a board setting written late

## Route

`Read` [references/protocol.md](references/protocol.md), then the playbook of the first row that fits.

| arguments | role | playbook |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `worker <name> manager <manager>`, then a url or the owner's words | worker | [references/worker.md](references/worker.md) |
| `sentinel <name> manager <manager>`, then a duty's words or url | sentinel | [references/sentinel.md](references/sentinel.md) |
| `succeed <name>` | manager | [references/manager.md](references/manager.md)'s Succession |
| anything else | manager | [references/manager.md](references/manager.md) |

Do each operation they name as [references/adapters.md](references/adapters.md) says for the adapter in use.

**Write it right once**: a board write passes its text as a file written first by the Write tool, never a bare `cat >` in a chained call, which waits on stdin until the call times out, and carries a title of at most 40 characters, since a hook denies the call otherwise and nothing runs.

**Stay in your worktree**: a worker never starts a command with `cd` into the live checkout, since a hook denies it; read that checkout by path or `git -C`.

**Edit a body by diff**: an issue body changes only by `edit-issue-body.py <issue> <diff-file> "DECIDED: <why>" --base <body sha>`, the diff file a unified diff of the body written first.

8	   - **Goal**: first answer what the owner wants to happen after this work, what a top professional would do, and what the work does, in verbs. `## Goal` states the owner's intent as objectives, scope and constraints, citing their words by url. Offer what widens it as a second option in the `REPORTED:` that files the task, since only the owner widens intent.
9	   - **Criteria**: `## Definition of done` holds one criterion per outcome of the routing `DECIDED:` and of each later `DECIDED:`, as [protocol.md](protocol.md) and [issue-grammar.md](issue-grammar.md) define them. One outcome never splits into several criteria; one scenario checks all its parts. Write each scenario the way its user would run the system.
10	   - **Lint**: fix every line [check-criteria.py](../scripts/check-criteria.py) `--task <n> <body-file>` prints, and every row [run-criteria.py](../scripts/run-criteria.py) `--base <body-file>` marks wrong, and with `--pass <n>=<sample-file>` for a `[check]` that pipes a producer into a tool, since the base run never reaches its pass path. Each line names its fix.
11	   - **Review**: a `judge` reviews the tasks. Then `comment` `REPORTED: task filed` on each, `tell` your manager its url, and build without waiting.
12	   - **Freeze**: after the first judge, change a criterion only as a manager's `DECIDED:` says, asked for by `BLOCKED:`. Fold the owner's decisions [list-additions.py](../scripts/list-additions.py) `<task>` lists in one `edit`, with `--base` of the `body sha` that `read` just printed. Close a judge's gap by fixing its cause, never by rewording or loosening a check.
13	2. **Build** each task on its own branch from the base, named as the repository's rules say and ending in `<your name>` or `<your name>-<word>`. Open the section of [build.md](build.md) for what the change touches: [Instructions](build.md#instructions), [Code](build.md#code), [UI](build.md#ui), [Migration](build.md#migration) or [Research](build.md#research).

Before each `judge`, run [run-criteria.py](../scripts/run-criteria.py) `<task>` at the head, fix each `fail` row, and `comment` its table on the task. import os
import pathlib
import sys
import time
from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone

sys.path.insert(0, str(pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "lib"))
import board  # noqa: E402
import landing  # noqa: E402
import session  # noqa: E402
import team_gaps  # noqa: E402
import team_names  # noqa: E402
import team_signal  # noqa: E402

POLL = float(os.environ.get("MONITOR_POLL", 60))  # the sessions are read each poll, which costs no GitHub points
REFRESH = float(os.environ.get("MONITOR_REFRESH", 900))  # a change made outside the team, such as the owner's comment on the web, sends no signal
SKEW = timedelta(seconds=5)  # GitHub's clock against ours


def read(manager, me, staffed, since):
    return team_gaps.manager_read(me, history=not staffed, since=since) if manager else team_gaps.worker_read(me)


def main(args):
    shown, staffed = set(), False  # the exit waits until this manager has had a worker, so a fresh manager routes first
    waiting = set()  # a worker's issues with an open blocker, so a restart reports no blocker closed long ago
    fed = set()  # the reports a manager was already fed
    data, read_at, signal = None, 0.0, team_signal.stamp()  # what GitHub last gave, when, and the signal file's change then
    while True:
        listed, me = session.sessions()
        role = team_names.role(me.get("name"))
        manager, worker = role == "manager", role == "worker"
        # GitHub is read when a team session signals a change or REFRESH has passed, and in full only when it first asks cheaply and something changed
        if (manager or worker) and (data is None or team_signal.stamp() != signal or time.time() - read_at >= REFRESH):
            now, seen = datetime.now(timezone.utc), team_signal.stamp()  # both taken before the read, so a touch during it still differs
            since = (datetime.fromtimestamp(read_at, timezone.utc) - SKEW).strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")
            checks = {board.changed_since, landing.changed_since}  # one function when both ports read GitHub, so its read runs once
            if data is None or any(check(since) for check in checks):
                data = read(manager, me, staffed, since if read_at else None)
            if data is not None:  # a failed read keeps the last good time, so the next read still feeds what came after it
                read_at, signal = now.timestamp(), seen
        lines = [] if not (manager or worker) else None if data is None else team_gaps.manager_actions(me, listed, data, fed) if manager else team_gaps.worker_actions(me, waiting, data)
        if manager and lines is not None:

"""Where a project keeps the data teamwork writes for itself: `<main checkout>/.teamwork/<name>`, the same for every worktree of the project."""
import pathlib
import subprocess


def common_folder():
    """The git common folder of the current folder's repository; None outside one, or with no git."""
    try:
        run = subprocess.run(["git", "rev-parse", "--path-format=absolute", "--git-common-dir"], capture_output=True, text=True)
    except OSError:
        return None
    return pathlib.Path(run.stdout.strip()) if run.returncode == 0 and run.stdout.strip() else None


def exclude(common, name):
    """Adds `/.teamwork/<name>/` to the common folder's `info/exclude`, so the data never reaches a commit while `.teamwork/settings.json` does."""
    line = f"/.teamwork/{name}/"
    path = common / "info" / "exclude"
    old = path.read_text() if path.exists() else ""
    if line not in old.splitlines():
        path.parent.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
        path.write_text(old + "\n" * bool(old and not old.endswith("\n")) + line + "\n")


def claim(common, name):
    """Moves a folder an older version kept in the common folder to the new place, never copied, since two copies would split the data."""
    old, new = common / "teamwork" / name, common.parent / ".teamwork" / name
    if old.is_dir() and not new.exists():
        new.parent.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
        old.rename(new)
        try:
            old.parent.rmdir()  # the folder an older version made, once nothing else is in it
        except OSError:
            pass

    """The folder for NAME, claimed on first use; None outside a repository, or with no git.
    A common folder that is not a `.git` (a bare repository, a submodule) keeps the data inside itself, where git never lists it."""
    common = common_folder()
    if common is None:
        return None
    if common.name != ".git":
        return common / "teamwork" / name
    claim(common, name)
    exclude(common, name)
    return common.parent / ".teamwork" / name
